extractions.quote: Electromyography showed continuous motor unit activity with normal morphology that was especially pronounced in lumbar paraspinal muscles and femoral muscles bilaterally. Myotonic potentials were absent. The activity resolved with benzodiazepines (10 mg diazepam i.v. ultrasonography over 1–2 min) (fig. 1). Simultaneous continuous motor activity was noted in opposing muscles. Electroneurography showed normal motor and sensory conductivity velocities for both common peroneal nerve and sural nerve, with normal compound muscle action potentials and sensory nerve action potentials amplitudes. F-wave latencies for common peroneal nerve and tibial nerve were normal bilaterally.

extractions.value: First report of autoimmune GAD65-positive SPS diagnosed in pregnancy. Caesarean section under general anaesthesia. Complete remission 2 weeks after delivery. Infant's serum anti-GAD65 negative.
extractions.quote: To our knowledge, this is the first report of a patient with autoimmune GAD65-positive SPS diagnosed in pregnancy. ... The patient gave birth to a healthy baby born at term by caesarean section under general anaesthesia. ... Complete remission was achieved in 2 weeks of the delivery. The anti-GAD65 titre in the infant's serum was negative.
